title: Church-centred life with few pianos or instruments
summary: Before any instruction he only listened to church singing; he notes the scarcity of pianos and that violins and trumpets were for white folks.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Up to that point, you hadn't had any musical instruction or anything?

I hadn't had any musical instructions until shortly there- I'll tell you, after, I hadn't reached that point,/but up 'til that time I had just listened, and I'd hear these gospel songs... very religious...well, I mean when I say very religious, I mean we went to church on Sundays. Sunday morning we had Sunday School, then the main service, then in the afternoon they would have some special singers coming, and after the singers, they would have the night service.

So you see that meant that you had a lot of time to hear a lot of singing and a majority of the ceremonies were songs. Dan , you know, I'm surprised today to hear people talk about how many great piano players there were during that period. I didn't see that many pianos. They had organs. There were small organs that you played with your foot, the tambourine, and the triangle. Those were the instruments that I saw. The violin, that was for white folks, and all that trumpet, and all that business. We had a few, but they were so rare, that it wasn't even worth even mentioning.
